newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Ports of Auckland sees subdued short term outlook.
newsitem.headline: Ports of Auckland sees subdued short term outlook.

text.p: Ports of Auckland Ltd Chairman Sir Richard Carter said on Monday the short term outlook for the company was subdued but was more promising in the long term.

Carter told the annual meeting that some economic activity had eased in the leadup to the October 12 general election. The continuing strength of the New Zealand dollar was also having an adverse impact on the volume of manufactured exports.
Volumes through the port had been static in the most recent quarter, although they had begun to pick up again since the end of September.
"But even if the short term outlook is subdued, we are comfortable about the long term prospects because of the increasing number of lines that hub on Auckland," he said.
Even on the most conservative estimates of ecomomic growth, container volumes were forecast to increase steadily over the long term.
Carter said greater competition on the Trans-Tasman route and the growth in coastal shpping in New Zealand were expected to reinforce Auckland's position as a hub port.
Ports of Auckland handled nearly 52 percent of New Zealand's total container trade in the year to June.
